title: Fibrewise regular equations give a flat slice over an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the last two properties tested on etale scheme charts. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ be a morphism from a field [def-weil-field], let $F=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $p:F\to X$. Let $r\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Fix a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to F$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and let $z$ be its image in $|F|$. The etale local ring $\mathcal O_{F,\bar z}$ means the stalk of the structure sheaf on the small etale site. If the images of the $f_i$ form a regular sequence in $\mathcal O_{F,\bar z}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], there is an open subspace $X_1\subset X$ containing $p(z)$ such that $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\cap X_1\to Y$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The closed subspace $V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is the zero locus of the ideal sheaf generated by these sections, formed on etale scheme charts [def-weil-closed-immersion]; open subspaces are formed on those charts as well [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 06LW (lemma-slice), including r=0; etale local ring as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 04KG (definition-etale-local-rings).

proof.text: Put $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. It is locally of finite presentation over $X$: on an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, its pullback has the presentation $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ with no extra variables and the displayed finite list of relations. Composition gives that $Z\to Y$ is locally of finite presentation, and its restrictions to open subspaces are as well. If $r=0$, then $Z=X$ and take $X_1=X$. Henceforth assume $r>0$.

source.place: Tag 06LW (lemma-slice), first paragraph; finite-equation presentation written explicitly.

proof.text: Choose surjective etale scheme charts $V\to Y$ and $U\to X\times_YV$. Then $U\to X$ is surjective etale, while $g:U\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation: $X\times_YV\to V$ is a base change of $f$, and the other factor is etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. The chart existence is part of the algebraic-space definition and the stability assertions are the cited calculus.

source.place: Tag 06LW, second paragraph: choose V and U.

proof.text: Use the given $k\to\Omega$ to put $F_\Omega=F\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The point $\bar z$ together with the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ gives an $\Omega$-point $z_\Omega$ of $F_\Omega$. Pull back the surjective etale chart $U\to X$ along this point. The resulting scheme $E\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is surjective etale, hence has a point $e$ and its canonical residue-field morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(e)\to E$. Apply the cited separably-closed lifting theorem with $L=\Omega$, extension field $\kappa(e)$, and the identity base point to obtain an $\Omega$-section of $E$. This gives a lift $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ of the prescribed map to $X$; let $u$ be its centre and let $v=g(u)$. Algebraic closure implies separable closure directly from the root condition.

source.place: Tag 06LW, field enlargement and lift through U; the given algebraically closed Omega supplies the enlargement.

proof.text: The projection $F_\Omega\to F$ is flat. On affine scheme charts it is induced by $A\to A\otimes_k\Omega$, which is faithfully flat by the field-extension lemma; the affine flatness criterion gives flatness of these charts. Consequently its map on etale local rings at $z_\Omega$ and $\bar z$ is flat and local, hence faithfully flat. Regular-sequence ascent gives regularity of the pulled-back $f_i$ in $\mathcal O_{F_\Omega,\bar z_\Omega}$.

source.place: Tag 06LW, field-extension paragraph; etale stalk flatness and regularity ascent.

proof.text: Put $H=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=U_v\times_{\kappa(v)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with pointed lift furnished by $\bar u$. Both $U\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to F_\Omega$ and $V\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are etale base changes of the chosen charts. The specified map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is etale by the between-etale-objects clause of the chartwise etale permanence lemma. Its base change is $H\to U\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Thus $H\to F_\Omega$ is etale. The strict-local comparison identifies its pointed etale local ring with that of $F_\Omega$, carrying each section $f_i$ to its pullback. The images of the $f_i$ are therefore regular in $C=\mathcal O_{H,\bar u}$.

source.place: Tag 06LW, the two etale arrows preceding the displayed local-ring map; use etale permanence in place of explicitly naming the diagonal.

proof.text: Let $R=\mathcal O_{U_v,u}$, and let $u_\Omega$ be the centre of the point on $H$. The map $R\to\mathcal O_{H,u_\Omega}$ is flat local: on affine pieces it is the localization of the faithfully flat field-extension map $A\to A\otimes_{\kappa(v)}\Omega$. The map $\mathcal O_{H,u_\Omega}\to C$ is faithfully flat by the strict-henselization theorem and the strict-local comparison. Transitivity gives a flat local map $R\to C$, which is faithfully flat. For $I_j=(f_1,\ldots,f_j)\subset R$, the quotient-tensor isomorphism gives $(R/I_j)\otimes_RC=C/I_jC$; universal injectivity embeds $R/I_j$ into this ring. If $f_{j+1}a=0$ in $R/I_j$, its image is zero under multiplication by $f_{j+1}$ in $C/I_jC$, so regularity in $C$ and that embedding force $a=0$. Also $R/I_r$ cannot be zero, since its tensor is the nonzero ring $C/I_rC$. This proves the required regular sequence in the ordinary fibre local ring $R$, including its nonzero-quotient clause.

source.place: Tag 06LW, displayed local-ring map and descent of regularity; Tag 00LM (lemma-flat-increases-depth), elementary kernel argument written out.

proof.text: Apply the scheme slicing input to $g:U\to V$, $u$, and the germs of the $f_i$: Step 2 gives local finite presentation and flatness at $u$, and Step 6 gives regularity in $\mathcal O_{U_v,u}$. Obtain an affine neighbourhood $W$ and representatives $a_i$ whose common zero locus is flat and locally of finite presentation over $V$. Each $a_i$ has the same germ as the already specified section $f_i|_W$. By the definition of a stalk there is a neighbourhood of $u$ on which these two sections agree; intersect the finitely many neighbourhoods. On this open $U'\subset W$, their zero loci agree, so $Z\times_XU'\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, by restriction to an open source.

source.place: Tag 06LW, application of the scheme slicing lemma; equality of the representatives is checked before taking the prescribed zero locus.

proof.text: Let $X_1\subset X$ be the open image of the etale map $U'\to X$. It contains the image of $u$, which is $p(z)$, and $U'\to X_1$ is surjective etale. Set $Z_1=Z\times_XX_1$. The map $D=Z\times_XU'\to Z_1$ is a surjective etale base change. On affine charts the equality with the zero locus of the pulled-back $f_i$ follows from $B\otimes_A A/(f_i)\cong B/(f_iB)$; hence this is the same $D$ proved flat over $V$ in Step 7, not merely a closed subset with that support.

source.place: Tag 06LW, final open-image construction and displayed square.

proof.text: The diagram $D\to V$ above $Z_1\to Y$ has surjective etale left vertical arrow and etale right vertical arrow. It is a chart diagram testing flatness, so the flatness of $D\to V$ proves that $Z_1\to Y$ is flat. Equivalently, at any point of $Z_1$ choose a point of its surjective etale chart $D$; the resulting scheme-chart map to $V$ is flat there, which is exactly the chartwise pointwise criterion. No claim that this diagram is cartesian is made. Local finite presentation was proved for all of $Z\to Y$ in Step 1, hence also holds on $Z_1$. Finally $Z_1=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\cap X_1$ by the specified closed-subspace construction, giving both conclusions.

source.place: Tag 06LW, final square and chartwise definition of flatness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06LW (lemma-slice), chart-reduction proof; explicit descent of regularity and equality of germs.
